name: game-win
origin: The one-player congratulations screen (OnePGameOverUI on PlayerGameOver, class UI_CONGRATULATIONSONEP) after the last level is won. As the results case (from tools/reference_player/cases/results/02-zero-kill-win-next.json: seed 42, Normal, Cinema, original AI.stop and controller.addBomb fixtures make the three enemies bomb themselves), with the five-levels option pressed (levelsFive's centre in the game-settings golden), which sets one level (GameSettingsUI.levelsHandle), so the first win is GAME_WIN: the score screen and its unlock tip (OK at okBt's centre), then NEXT (nextLevel's centre) opens the congratulations screen (PlayerScoreUI.nextLevelFunc -> UIManager.gameOver). realtime 1 lets the original timers run on wall time. Checkpoint 3.
godot_note: Godot replays the menus and the score screen with the same clicks; the round is settled by the Godot-only `settle` action with the recorded final score.

actions.godot_note: Godot cannot play the original round: it ends here as the last level won, with the final score the original's congratulations screen showed (App.settle_as_recorded); the score screen, its unlock tip and NEXT are then replayed with the same clicks.

actions.godot_why: owner edit: the score screen moves NEXT left by 96.7, half the way from DRESS UP to MORE GAMES (tools/convert/owner_edits.json)
